speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing the history. To better understand your condition, could you tell me how long you have been experiencing this neck and arm pain, and does it radiate in a specific pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: That progression from burning pain to actual weakness is concerning for nerve compression. Given your history of diabetes and the radiation of symptoms, have you noticed any difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts or holding a glass? Also, have you experienced any numbness in the groin or buttocks area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Anterior Horn Cell involvement (Cervical Spondylomyelopathy).

REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI_with_contrast.

REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Study_and_Electromyography (EMG).
